turn_text: I'm Anna Rocha with a brief look at the latest news in Texas politics and policy from the Texas Tribune. Reaction from Congress to President Donald Trump's decision to withdraw the United States from the Iran nuclear deal fell mostly along party lines with Texas Democrats condemning the move and Republicans applauding it. But at least one key Texas conservative, Congressman Mac Thornberry, the highest-ranking House Republican on national defense issues, said while he didn't doubt the deal was flawed, the president should have waited longer to see if European allies could have improved the terms. After Trump took office, Texas counties were some of the most compliant when it came to working with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, according to a new report published by the Migration Policy Institute. In Harris County alone, from January to May of 2017, the number of inmates transferred to federal immigration authorities custody jumped 60%. That was before the state legislature had even passed its sanctuary city's law. Elsewhere, Bayer and Webb counties complied with every detain or request. while Dallas officials declined 17, and Travis County declined 130. As the temperatures heat up across the state, prisoners serving time in Wallace-Pack prison, southeast of College Station, can rest assured they'll have air conditioning to keep them cool. Tuesday, a U.S. District Judge ended a years-long lawsuit over prison heat conditions and finalized a settlement proposal that includes permanently installing air conditioning at the prison. The Texas Department of Criminal Justice installed temporary air conditioning at the unit earlier this year to cover the next two summers. This summer, the nation's first driverless cars will be navigating the streets of a Dallas Fort Worth suburb. Read more now at TexasTribune.org. I'm Alana Rocha with the Texas Tribune. You've been briefed. The brief is presented by the Office of Public Insurance Council. Confused about what insurance coverage is right for you? Try our policy comparison tool at opic.texas.gov.
